title: Ephemeral VRAM leak chase notes
content:
Note-to-self: trying to capture the odd OOM that shows up after ~6-12 hours of a steady workload. Behavior summary:

- Symptoms: process (python worker) hits CUDA OOM during small allocation (~50MB) even though nvidia-smi reports ~2-4 GB free. Memory step-up appears gradual across hours. A restart of the python process does NOT recover — need to reboot the node or unload+reload driver (rmmod/nvidia) to free the VRAM.

- Suspected class: driver / persistent context leak OR memory pinned outside of CUDA runtime (kernel/NVML/ibverbs) OR fragmentation causing failures even with free memory. Also possible: hidden persistent contexts from containerd/runc shim or other stray process holding device contexts.

Raw timeline notes (observational):
- 2026-02-17 03:20: normal traffic, 8 python worker containers on node gpu-07 (A100-80GB).
- 2026-02-17 09:45: first OOM reported from worker-3 during a small decode op.
- 2026-02-17 09:46: watched nvidia-smi for 30m — total GPU memory shown used stays ~72GB used / 8GB free. But python process shows low resident RSS (~3.2GB).
- 2026-02-17 10:05: restarted python worker -> immediate CUDA init on restart increases used memory by ~1.2GB (expected), but total used still anomalously high.
- 2026-02-17 11:00: rebooting other non-gpu services did nothing; only driver reload or full node reboot clears the leak.

Commands tried and outputs (cut/paste style):

1) nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
[NVIDIA-SMI output trimmed]
GPU 0:
    FB Memory Usage
        Total                       : 81920 MiB
        Used                        : 72416 MiB
        Free                        : 9504 MiB

2) ps aux | grep python (in container)
root      12345  1.2  4.1 1234560 325000 ?     Ssl  09:00   0:40 python -u worker.py
-> process RSS 318M inside container (top shows small).

3) sudo lsof /dev/nvidia* | wc -l
-> a handful of file handles from containerd + worker processes. No obvious orphan.

4) cat /proc/12345/smaps | egrep "^Size:|^Rss:|^Private_Dirty:" | sed -n '1,20p'
-> python process shows small private mappings; nothing near GPU FB size.

5) nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo via python (pynvml):
import pynvml
...
# returns same view as nvidia-smi: total=81920, free=9504, used=72416

6) sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia*
-> shows expected pids (containerd-shim, worker pids). No zombies.

7) docker stats / crictl top container: memory cgroup < 4GB; confirms userspace not holding the missing 60+GB.

8) strace -e mmap -p 12345 (attached briefly) -> no huge allocations visible.

9) grep -i "cuCtx" in /var/log/messages + dmesg -> nothing obvious, but kernel shows repeated WARNs about TTM memory pressure (could be unrelated).

10) nvidia-smi pmon -c 1 -> process IDs listed do not sum to used memory.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: CUDA driver holds long-lived allocations tied to a persistent context that survives process restarts (e.g., via container runtime shim, rmmod race). Some daemon is creating contexts and not releasing them.
- H2: Memory fragmentation in GPU FB causing allocation failure despite global free memory. The allocator can't find contiguous block for requested allocation.
- H3: NVML or driver leaked pinned pages into kernel (e.g., via IB verbs/pinned RDMA pages), which are not visible to process smaps.
- H4: MPS or similar service (not in our stack) created contexts across users.
- H5: CUDA driver bug in this driver version (510.x-ish) interacting with certain cuDNN/cuBLAS calls that leak on context switch.

Experiments performed and quick conclusions:
- Created a tiny reproducer that repeatedly allocates 1GB Torch tensors and frees them in a loop from within container (python). Observed that after ~400 iterations, cudaMalloc fails although nvidia-smi still shows ~8-9GB free. Conclusion: leak / fragmentation at driver-level.
- Restarting containerd-shim for the container sometimes freed some memory (weird), but not reliably.
- Unloading nvidia kernel modules (rmmod nvidia_uvm; rmmod nvidia_drm; rmmod nvidia) freed all GPU memory; implies driver-level allocations.
- Running same loop on local dev machine with different driver (525.x) did NOT leak -> driver-version correlation.

Quick repro script (not bulletproof):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import torch, time
for i in range(10000):
    a = torch.empty((256,1024,1024), dtype=torch.float32, device='cuda')
    a = None
    if i%50==0:
        print(i, torch.cuda.memory_allocated(), torch.cuda.memory_reserved())
    time.sleep(0.1)

Notes: the above is aggressive; used to provoke fragmentation. On offending nodes allocation errors start appearing after many iterations even though torch.cuda reports small reserved numbers.

Additional diagnostic commands to run next time an incident occurs (to capture before reboot):
- sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/dri/0/nvidia_memory
- sudo nvtop (snapshot)
- sudo grep -R "nvidia" /proc/*/maps | head -n 200 (to find any hidden mappings)
- for pid in $(pidof containerd-shim); do sudo ls -l /proc/$pid/fd | wc -l; done -> FD counts may show leaked handles
- /usr/bin/strace -f -tt -e trace=open,close,ioctl -p <pid_of_shim> (capture ioctl calls to NV driver)
- dumpcu (internal script) to enumerate contexts via nvidia-smi/driver APIs (TODO: script this)
- nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses and nvmlDeviceGetGraphicsRunningProcesses (from pynvml) every 30s to see if process list changes while memory used climbs
- sudo sh -c 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' (unlikely to affect GPU but quick to try)

Workarounds used in prod temporarily:
- Cron job: nightly node reboot on affected GPU fleet (gross but effective).
- Limit worker lifetime to 6 hours (rotate containers), this reduces incidence but doesn't fix root cause.
- Set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32 to reduce fragmentation (helped marginally).

Questions for escalation to driver/vendor teams:
- Are there known leaks in driver 510.47.x when contexts are created in nested container/shim environments?
- Is there a way to enumerate persistent contexts that are not tied to a pid (NVML/DRM debug interfaces)?
- Can NV driver hold pinned pages for RDMA that are invisible to userland processes?
- Does our orchestration create any long-running privileged process that might create GPU contexts (e.g., device-health-check, telemetry, NCCL daemons)?

Notes on what to avoid during next incident (to preserve evidence):
- Don't reboot or reload modules until we capture: nvml snapshots, /proc/*/maps, containerd-shim FDs, and kmsg.
- Avoid restarting containerd or docker unless trying as an experiment and capturing state first.

Next steps (practical):
- Add nvml snapshot cron that logs memory counts and process lists every 5 minutes for suspect nodes (log retention 7 days).
- Add wrapper to worker startup that records driver versions, module versions, kmsg snapshot.
- Try upgrade to 525.x on a staging node and run long-run repro (compare).
- Create a small C repro that uses CUDA Driver API (not runtime) and creates/destroys contexts quickly to test for leaks at driver-level. If driver-level repro leaks -> vendor ticket.
- Add a nightly job that does 'nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0' for devices that support it (safer than full reboot).

Useful references / remind-me links:
- TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF docs: https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html
- pynvml samples: https://pypi.org/project/pynvml/
- NVidia developer forum threads on "cuda OOM while nvidia-smi shows free" (search: OOM vs free)

Random breadcrumbs / things I wrote while sleepy:
- Could be a pattern where a small number of large allocations are getting split into many pinned blocks -> fragmentation. If driver free list holds many small ranges, kernel fails to coalesce.
- Check if any of our monitoring agents (node-exporter with nvidia plugin) open long-lived contexts for metrics sampling. (Node-exporter has a GPU plugin in some setups.)

Logs appended (trimmed):
[worker stderr]
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/worker.py", line 298, in process_batch
    logits = model.generate(inputs)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 64.00 MiB (GPU 0; 79.68 GiB total capacity; 4.22 GiB already allocated; 64.00 MiB free; 4.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

Note: message says 64MB free but nvidia-smi shows ~9GB free. This discrepancy is the core symptom.

If I get a clean repro that consistently leaks, escalate to vendor with: driver version, dmesg, nvml snapshots, small C driver-API repro.

End of notes. Keep this doc as living scratchpad. Will copy important steps to a Confluence page if we get reproducible steps.
